
```{r}
# Great Work Azzedine !

view(world_countries)
view(clean_csv)

# We just need to enhance something ... joining over names of countries columns will cause underlying errors ! from the first look we can see (Bolivia) in world_countries called "Bolivia (Plurinational State of) " and in clean_csv its called "Bolivia" so the join will fail silently over this case ): 

# The problem is our primary key (Identifier) is different between the two DSs one uses iso 3 and the other uses iso 2 BUT!

# our solution will come from the library called "library(countrycode)" which can change iso 2 to iso 3 or vice versa

library(countrycode)

clean_csv <- my_csv %>%
  
  #Also lets clean out the totals rows that start with the string pattern "ZZ"
  
  filter(!str_detect(iso3, "^ZZ")) %>%         
  
  select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) %>%
  
  mutate(diff_2019_2010 = gii_2019 - gii_2010,iso2 = countrycode(iso3, origin = "iso3c", destination = "iso2c")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff_2019_2010))

clean_csv

# Join on ISO codes instead of names

final_map <- world_countries |>
  left_join(clean_csv, by = c("ISO" = "iso2"))

final_map



sum(is.na(final_map$diff_2019_2010))
```

```{r}
#Lets Plot a simple map

library(tmap)

tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(final_map) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "diff_2019_2010") +
  tm_title("Change in Gender Inequality Index, 2010–2019")

#I know its not the best MAP but it is suffiecient enough :)))
```
